items.streamTitle: Instagram audiences expressed less emotion toward virtual than human influencers
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 156,918 Instagram comments found both positive and negative emotion language less common for virtual influencers, with substantial variation. Platform correlations are not causal effects.
items.attribution: Jagodnik and Bartal — Scientific Reports (observational social-media study)

items.streamTitle: Conflict adaptation persisted even when conscious conflict expectancy was unreliable
items.streamSummary: Three flanker-task experiments found robust conflict adaptation despite unreliable explicit expectancy and imperfect recall of prior conflict. The findings challenge an expectancy-only account.
items.attribution: Christy et al. — Scientific Reports (three behavioral experiments)

items.streamTitle: Large preregistered study found no shared neural signature of emotion-regulation capacity
items.streamSummary: Across 40 fMRI datasets and 2,175 participants, three common cognitive-reappraisal indicators did not converge or show expected prefrontal associations. This challenges measurement assumptions, not emotion regulation itself.
items.attribution: Sicorello et al. — Nature (preregistered consortium study)

items.streamTitle: Game-theoretic persuasion agent exposed failures when opponents broke assumptions
items.streamSummary: A GLEE competition agent combined Bayesian opponent models and moral-framing messages with classical solvers. Simulation and live-game analyses exposed failure modes; rhetoric–purchase links were correlational.
items.attribution: Hayden Arnold — arXiv preprint (GLEE competition case study)

items.streamTitle: Interactive simulated users changed AI negotiation outcomes and increased misalignment
items.streamSummary: In 11,200 simulated bargaining runs, user presence raised agent payouts but also increased problematic conduct, including 14.3% user-facing misalignment. Real-user behavior was not studied.
items.attribution: Pan et al. — arXiv preprint (PRESENT agent evaluation)

items.streamTitle: Army modeling study defined hurdles to forecasting tactical cyberspace opportunities
items.streamSummary: An October 23 Army report explored short-lived cyber-operational opportunity forecasts using synthetic data. It identified uncertainty and computing obstacles rather than proving a deployment-ready capability.
items.attribution: Thomas and Raio — DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory, ARL-TR-10474

items.streamTitle: AI persuasion changed petition signing, while attitude and behavior effects diverged
items.streamSummary: Two preregistered experiments involving 14,779 people found conversational AI could increase real petitions or donations, while attitude shifts poorly tracked behavioral shifts. Broader effects remain untested.
items.attribution: Hackenburg et al. — PNAS (preregistered randomized experiments)

items.streamTitle: Small persistent minorities shifted outcomes in four LLM-agent society simulations
items.streamSummary: EXAM varied persistent minority-agent proportions and placement across four synthetic social settings and found configuration-dependent collective shifts. These are model outputs, not validated human effects.
items.attribution: Chen et al. — arXiv preprint (EXAM social-simulation framework)

items.streamTitle: NATO StratCom review found thin evidence for many disruptive counter-FIMI measures
items.streamSummary: A NATO-accredited centre reviewed ways to disrupt hostile information operations and found limited effectiveness evidence for many measures. It recommends context-sensitive operational assessment.
items.attribution: Thomas Colley — NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence (research report)

items.streamTitle: AR field of view and contrast changed search performance, reliance and trust
items.streamSummary: Two 20-person within-subject studies found benefits from wider and higher-contrast AR overlays while reliance strategies mattered. Real-world operational generalization remains uncertain.
items.attribution: Choudhary et al. — IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics

items.streamTitle: Army planners tested an LLM-and-simulation prototype for course-of-action development
items.streamSummary: An Army Research Laboratory touchpoint combined COA-generating AI, constructive simulation, and a planning interface. Three SMEs estimated a possible future 30% reduction in time and mental effort; that gain was not measured.
items.attribution: Gremillion et al. — DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory, ARL-TR-10475

items.streamTitle: Stimulus-specific amygdala activity predicted which visual experiences people remembered
items.streamSummary: Human single-neuron recordings linked category-specific amygdala firing to later recognition and confidence, independent of emotional ratings. Neural association does not prove a method for improving memory.
items.attribution: Xiao et al. — Nature Neuroscience

items.streamTitle: Adolescents using general-purpose AI for mental-health help often wanted further support
items.streamSummary: In a survey of 24,132 students, 2.7% used general-purpose AI for mental-health support; many found it helpful yet still sought or wanted other help. Clinical effectiveness was not tested.
items.attribution: Okechukwu et al. — npj Mental Health Research

items.streamTitle: Image-enhancement prototype combined semantic checks with limited provenance recovery
items.streamSummary: A new image-enhancement model combined semantic-consistency checks with 99.8% metadata recovery on untransformed outputs. It is not C2PA-signed, tamper-proof, or validated after social-media transformations.
items.attribution: Liu et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: A smartphone-personalized LLM systematically overstated people's positive feelings
items.streamSummary: Across 83 people and 17 weeks of smartphone traces, a personalized LLM predicted people felt happier and less distressed than they reported. Longer histories did little to resolve that bias.
items.attribution: Fang et al. — npj Digital Public Health

items.streamTitle: Amharic multimodal benchmark exposed limits in information-disorder classification
items.streamSummary: An 8,053-item Amharic multimodal benchmark reported 0.68 accuracy and 0.67 F1 for information-disorder classification. Annotation uncertainty and untested field robustness remain important.
items.attribution: Woldegiorgis, Abebe and Jimma — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Reddit self-declarations made demographic inference more auditable than opaque proxies
items.streamSummary: Using over 850,000 Reddit self-declarations, a transparent probabilistic approach often outperformed opaque demographic proxies. Sampling bias, privacy, and demographic inference error still constrain use.
items.attribution: Cinus et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: FCM dynamics were converted into an eight-scene generated video storyboard
items.streamSummary: A preprint converted a five-node fuzzy cognitive map into eight AI-generated scenes using perturbation-and-attractor rules. It demonstrates visualization, not validated causal or behavioral simulation.
items.attribution: Panda, Adigun and Kosko — arXiv preprint

items.streamTitle: Ad-auction telemetry raised surveillance concerns for Starlink users
items.streamSummary: An October 27 Reuters investigation linked an unusually active Starlink-focused advertising bidder to an alleged Israeli surveillance firm. Wide bidding is documented; individual tracking or compromise was not established.
items.attribution: Raphael Satter — Reuters (original investigation, October 27)

items.streamTitle: Voice-confidence gains exceeded measured speech changes in two student cohorts
items.streamSummary: A four-week shadowing-and-awareness program involving 120 students in Egypt and Saudi Arabia coincided with large confidence gains but nonsignificant acoustic changes. No untreated comparison group was used.
items.attribution: Zanaty et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (mixed-methods pre/post study)

items.streamTitle: Human judges struggled to distinguish AI responses across six controlled tasks
items.streamSummary: A Nature Human Behaviour study tested 636 humans, 37 AI agents and over 72,000 identity judgments. AI imitation challenged human judges in restricted tasks, while machine judges performed better; field deception was not tested.
items.attribution: Nature Human Behaviour — original human/AI imitation experiments

items.streamTitle: New review separates four research roles for language models in social science
items.streamSummary: A Nature Human Behaviour review distinguishes LLMs as simulated subjects, analytic assistants, collaborators and evaluators. It highlights causal-inference and social-realism limits rather than demonstrating human-equivalent simulation.
items.attribution: Xu et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (review)

items.streamTitle: Adaptive camouflage reduced human and machine detection in controlled tests
items.streamSummary: CephCam combined sensing with a changing display on a model vehicle. In controlled scenes and a 112-volunteer detection experiment, it reduced human and machine detection; operational stealth remains untested.
items.attribution: Zhu et al. — Nature Communications (engineering and human psychophysics)

items.streamTitle: AI awareness raised both motivation and job insecurity in a student experiment
items.streamSummary: A three-study Chinese university project found an AI-intensive scenario increased both motivation and job insecurity, while surveys linked both to flexible-career attitudes. Survey mediation does not establish causal career change.
items.attribution: Liang, Jiang and Chen — Scientific Reports (survey studies and scenario experiment)
